design.aa_rule: an A/A pair is one B side and one Baa side with the same point and the rank seed of primary pair j (j = 1..K_AA). The 2 K_AA sides alternate strictly, with the start drawn from the same generator
design.pair_rule: a primary pair is one A side and one B side with the same point and the same rank seed. Each point's K pairs run as 2K sides in strict alternation, ABAB... or BABA..., and the starting side is drawn from random.Random(ORDER_SEED0 + i). Pair j is sides 2j-1 and 2j
design.planted_rule: a planted pair is kM38I and kM38IX, rank processes only, with the rank seed of primary pair K. They alternate, and the start is drawn from the same generator
design.process_model: one point per process, fresh process per run, one pinned CPU, one runner
design.rank_seeds_note: 1201-1230 are new on n=83. Used before: 7, 29, 101-102, 201-204, 301-309, 401-404, 501-504, 701, 801-816, 901-904 and 1101-1116 (every protocol on origin and in the scratch worktrees). Each seed fixes K' new rank targets [a]G - R_c on each base

design.runtime_estimate: power.json runtime: about 163 min for the job (149 min schedule), about 243 min on a 1.5x slower host; the job limit is 300 min
design.segment_rule: O1: Q0 on cPI and cM38I, shuffled by random.Random(ORDER_SEED0 + 99). Then one segment P<i> per point i = 1..POINTS in panel order. Its four sub-blocks (primary, aa, planted, rho) run in an order shuffled by the point's generator
design.side_rule: a side is two fresh processes run back to back, its rank process and then its cold process, both on the pair's point. The rank process runs the rank stage with the pair's rank seed and then solves the point. The cold process loads the base's verified table and solves the point
design.time_guard: before each segment: skip it (rows skipped_time_guard) if the elapsed job time plus the larger of its upper estimate and 1.1x the longest segment of its panel so far exceeds 285 min. A skipped row makes the run invalid

exactness_argument: Frobenius phi acts on the prime-order subgroup as multiplication by lambda (lambda^2 - lambda + 2 = 0 mod r), so for alpha = a + b tau, alpha(R) = [a]R + [b]phi(R) = [(a + b lambda) mod r]R, and every member +-phi^k(alpha(R_c)) of orbit (c, alpha) has discrete log +-(a + b lambda) lambda^k log R_c. The header carries exactly these labels; verify_closure.py re-derives every member and label from the orbit representative and checks each representative against [w]R_c and, with the table, against [w L_c]G, in the pinned oracle. A relation found by the unchanged S3 search is checked in the group by the unchanged lift (four base points summing to the attempt's point), so its row sum_i coeff_i L_{c_i} = a (+ L_c for the guided column) holds exactly; full rank gives the unique logs, checked [L_c]G = R_c in process and equal to B's archived logs of the same R_c. A target's scalar is checked [d]G = Q in process and replayed in the oracle, and must equal the baseline's and the tuned rho's. The root index, probe loop and scan are the rank-probe producer's code, built from the closure's orbit representatives. With KIC_INDEX_CANON=lift the index build keys every stored state's two normal-basis roots with lift_scan instead of the selected canonicalizer; both return the least rotation of the 83-bit word and the least shift reaching it, the stored states are computed before and independently of that call, so the table receives the same inserts in the same order and its slot array is the same word for word (index-lift's argument). The layout digests gate this per process on every base, so every relation, probe count, rank table and scalar of a lift-built index is the selected-built index's.
expected_effect: about 7.66 end to end at the parent run's means (power_check.py expected_ratio_at_prior_means; an estimate, not a claim)
gates: every scheduled row present and valid (exit 0, verified, schedule match, no memory event), no time-guard skip

Rows ran in schedule order. runner_start.json records this protocol's, this schedule's, arm.py's and run_schedule.py's SHA-256 and no smoke subset. Every row ran the binary runner_start.json records, unchanged at the end. An unknown gate is a failure

question: Replication of PR #997 under the Tier 1 rule. Is the closure + index-lift M38I producer's END-TO-END cold cost (setup + index build + rank stage + linear algebra + one-target online) lower than the index-lift row's on new held-out points and new rank seeds? The test uses repeated alternating pairs and a 95% paired confidence interval whose lower bound must exceed 1 (AGENTS.md, 'CPU performance isolation gate', Tier 1). Every relation is checked in the group, every column log and scalar verified, the probe law kept, and the index-lift layout reproduced byte for byte.

statistics.e2e_per_side: E2E(side) = timing_ms.rank_stage of the side's rank process + cold_in_process_ms of the side's cold process. The cold process holds setup + index build + online, the rank stage holds the rank attempts and the linear algebra. So E2E = setup + index build + rank stage + linear algebra + one-target online, the row's definition
statistics.pairing_basis: AGENTS.md Tier 1: 'run both variants on the same pinned exposed CPU with the same workload and limits' and 'require repeated alternating pairs'. A pair is the two variants on the same point with the same rank seed, adjacent in time on one CPU, in alternating order. docs/IC_BENCHMARK_TIERS.md uses the same unit (the same point, alternating order, one allocation)
statistics.primary: R = sum over the 30 primary pairs of E2E(A) / sum over the same pairs of E2E(B). 95% percentile interval from a two-stage paired bootstrap, 10000 draws, random.Random(20261020): the points drawn with replacement, then each drawn point's pairs drawn with replacement; A and B of a pair are always drawn together
statistics.primary_is: the paired END-TO-END ratio; the rank-stage and cold ratios are co-reported and never decide
secondary: geometric mean of the per-pair ratios E2E(A)/E2E(B), with the same bootstrap
rank stage kPI / kM38I and cold cPI / cM38I, both paired, with the same bootstrap
E2E process CPU time (user + system of both processes of each side) A / B, with the same bootstrap
E2E process wall time (both processes of each side) A / B, with the same bootstrap
per-point ratio, and the ratio by pair position in the sequence (first, second, ...) and by side order
setup, index build, online and peak RSS cPI / cM38I over the primary pairs
probe law of kPI and kM38I; rows without gain; point-addition counters
rho ms/step from rT; S per arm; E2E cold gap IC / rT

success_criterion: AGENTS.md 'Success criterion: iterative improvement of the index-calculus baseline'
tier_rule: AGENTS.md 'CPU performance evidence tiers', Tier 1: same pinned exposed CPU, same workload and limits; code and workload hashes, paired order, raw failures, correctness, process CPU time, memory, cgroup throttling and memory failures, steal time and scheduling counters recorded; repeated alternating pairs and a 95% paired confidence interval whose lower bound exceeds 1
why_this_run: PR #997 (merged e55510070) made this producer the n=83 a=1 row: 7.6558 [7.2192, 8.1103], run 39335956567. Its primary had one cM38I and one cPI cold observation per point (20 points) and separate rank blocks (4 kPI, 16 kM38I). Neither the cold arms nor the rank arms were repeated alternating primary pairs, so the row does not rest on a qualified Tier 1 speedup (the owner's qualification notes on claude/n83-knownlog and claude/n83-onlineframe make the same point for PRs #986 and #988). This run replicates it properly.
